title: GPU Procurement: Commitment & Pricing Playbook (Q3–Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook documents negotiation levers, contract templates, decision thresholds, and short-term tactics for GPU procurement commitments and structured pricing for Q3–Q4 2026. It is intended for the infra procurement lead, finance counterpart, and the serving-runtime engineering stakeholder who needs capacity forecasts factored into committed spend.

Executive summary:

We expect a tightening window between July and October driven by several model onboarding milestones and increased Dedicated customer activity. The objective of this playbook is to secure a blended procurement strategy that: 1) locks favorable unit economics for baseline capacity (committed), 2) retains optionality for peak demand (on-demand/spot/reserve windows), and 3) embeds contractual SLA/repair/expedite clauses to reduce lead-time risk.

Key negotiation levers (order of priority):

- Commitment volume tiers: negotiate stepped pricing where price per unit drops at 3 breakpoints (small, medium, large). Aim for minimum 10% discount vs public list at small tier and 18–25% at large tier.
- Delivery windows and partial shipments: insist on split-delivery lanes with at least 30% of committed units available in first tranche within 8–12 weeks, remainder on controlled schedule.
- Price indexation and cap: require fixed pricing for first six months post-PO and a cap on any indexation thereafter tied to a mutually agreed semiconductor price index.
- Force majeure and substitution: include explicit SKU substitution rules (compatible specs, equivalent or better FP performance) and pre-approved substitution list to avoid delays.
- Penalties and credits: negotiate delivery SLAs with credits that scale from 2–8% of tranche value for missed windows beyond agreed grace period.
- Spare parts and RMA turnarounds: mandate local repair spares pool or guaranteed RMA turnaround <21 days for critical SKUs.
- Early termination/rollout flexibility: limited exit option if a vendor cannot meet 60% of committed delivery by agreed mid-point; include replenishment support clause.

Pricing mechanics and amortization guidance:

- Capitalization vs OPEX: for Dedicated Reserved pools we amortize committed spend over contract term (usually 12 months) for unit economics; capture break-even token price and effective per-token cost at 70%/85% utilization scenarios.
- True-up and settlement: prefer quarterly true-up where adjustments are based on actual usage buckets; avoid monthly per-unit true-ups that increase overhead.
- Freight & import duties: push vendor to include freight-to-region pricing in committed unit cost; otherwise require transparent line-item duties and delayed billing disallowed beyond 60 days post-delivery.

SKU substitution and compatibility matrix (operational rule-of-thumb):

- Preferred SKUs: A100-80GB (or equivalently characterized Ampere derivatives), H100-80GB, and next-gen X series if price/perf meets our validated profiles.
- Substitution rules: allows +/-10% in memory bandwidth or FP32 TFLOPs if latency/per-token benchmarks validated by our serving-runtime team. Any substitution must pass a 48-hour smoke test on a defined benchmark.

Decision matrix for commitment size (high-level):

Inputs: 12-month demand forecast, percent attributable to Dedicated contracts, runway for new model rollouts, expected median sequence length.
- If forecasted steady-state demand < 40 GPUs/month: avoid 12-month hard commitment; negotiate small tranche + options.
- If forecast between 40–150 GPUs/month: pursue medium-tier commitment with 6–9 month ramp and hold 15–25% buffer in spot/market.
- If forecast > 150 GPUs/month or significant enterprise deals pending: pursue large commitment with staged delivery and SLA-backed credits.

Risk scenarios and mitigation playbook:

1) Vendor lead-time slip: trigger short-term marketplace purchases (spot/reserve) plus cross-region borrow; escalate to vendor management to invoke penalty clauses. Maintain 8% of committed capacity as float inventory at any time.
2) Price spike mid-contract: capped indexation clause + pre-negotiated spot-purchase allotment for overflow. Finance to review hedging instruments if exposure > $2M/quarter.
3) SKU EOL / obsolescence: substitution clause plus technical sign-off window. For critical SKUs maintain a 6-month retirement runway.
4) Logistics/ports delay for a region: fallback to alternate region shipments; require vendor to pay for expedited cross-region air freight for critical tranches.

Operational checklist for procurement run: (to be used by buyer and infra PM)

- Validate 12-month forecast with product and sales (attach forecast worksheet).
- Identify primary and secondary vendors (contact matrix below).
- Define tranche schedule and map to expected release dates in infra calendar.
- Run vendor quote comparison sheet (TTM price, lead-time, RMA terms, early-payment discounts).
- Legal to insert SLA/caps/penalty language; procurement to keep negotiation scorecard.
- If early delivery required, confirm logistics capacity & customs windows 30 days prior.

Vendor contact matrix (kept minimal here; full list in Confluence):

- Vendor A (global OEM reseller): primary for H100 and A100-family. Primary contact: Ravi Mehra (procurement lead) -> r.mehera@vendorA.com.
- Vendor B (regional distributor APAC/EU): best lead-times for small tranches. Primary contact: Asha Patel -> a.patel@vendorb.com.

Templates and artifacts to attach to RFQ:

- Standard tranche schedule (sample table with dates and percentages).
- Contract clause snippets: SKU substitution, price cap, RMA SLA, partial shipment, credit schedule.
- Negotiation scorecard (price / lead-time / SLAs / RMAs / spare parts / early-payment discount).

Open questions / To discuss:

- How aggressive should we be on early-payment discounts vs preserving cash runway? (Finance input required).
- For next-gen SKU pilots (X-series), who funds validation runs and where do we record performance deltas?
- Should we increase float inventory from 8% to 12% ahead of the major model rollout in September?

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):

- Finalize forecast reconciliation: Product + Sales -> due 2026-02-16 (owner: Diego Alvarez).
- Issue RFQ to Vendor A/B/C: procurement -> 2026-02-20 (owner: Maya Thompson).
- Legal to draft standard clause language for review: legal -> 2026-02-24 (owner: Priya Sharma).
- Run cost amortization scenarios and utilization sensitivity: finance -> 2026-02-28 (owner: Jonah Kim).

Appendix (quick reference):

- Benchmarks required for substitution approval: 1) 95th-percentile per-token latency at target batch size, 2) memory usage profile and KV cache behavior, 3) power efficiency stat for region thermal planning.
- Template credit schedule: 0–7 day slip = warning; 8–21 day slip = 2% credit per tranche per week; >21 day slip escalate to senior vendor management for arbitration and 8% tranche credit cap.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working doc — comments welcome in-line or via the procurement Slack thread. If you are an engineering stakeholder, flag any SKU that will require additional validation time; include benchmark tag in replies so we can prioritize smoke-test resources.
